feature: Math.toBase(n: number, base: number): string is a bespoke (invented) built-in added under the Math namespace. Because it lives on Math (typed as `any` by the static type checker), no TypeSystem change is needed: Math.toBase(255, 16) type-checks as any. The reference implementation registers a MethodV2("toBase", 2, ...) entry on the BuiltInStaticBuilder chain in MathBuiltIns.cs plus one private helper method ToBase(double, double) on the same class that returns a C# string wrapped in RuntimeValue.FromString.
reference_approach: Truncate both arguments to integers (long value, int radix).
Validate radix is 2..16 (throw otherwise); the hidden tests never exercise an out-of-range base, so this is defensive only.
Determine sign, then accumulate the unsigned magnitude with repeated modulo/divide by radix, prepending each digit. Use the digit table "0123456789abcdef" so 10..15 map to lowercase a..f.
Prepend '-' if the original value was negative.
Return RuntimeValue.FromString(result). SharpTS prints the string as-is via console.log.
registration_note: The key discovery the agent must make: built-ins are NOT added via a TypeSystem/AST change. They are registered as MethodV2 entries on the fluent BuiltInStaticBuilder in MathBuiltIns.cs (see existing abs/floor/pow/min). Putting toBase under Math means the type checker treats the call as `any`, so it compiles and runs without touching Parsing/TypeSystem. The method returns a STRING, so use RuntimeValue.FromString rather than FromNumber.
edge_cases_most_likely_missed: Negative numbers: a naive `while (n > 0)` loop on a negative input returns "" or loops wrong; correct behavior is a single leading '-' then the magnitude (c4 -2a, c9 -11111111, c11 -1, c14 -100).
Zero: a `while (n > 0)` loop produces "" instead of "0" (c3).
Digits above 9 must be LOWERCASE a-f. Off-by-one ascii mapping (e.g. char('0'+d) for d>9 yields ':',';'...) or uppercase A-F both fail (c1 ff, c4 2a, c10 ab, c12 3e8).
Base 2 and base 16 boundaries: single hex digit 15->f vs two-digit 16->10 (c7, c8); base-2 widths (c2, c5).

v1.note: happy-path repro; fails on baseline (Math.toBase undefined -> runtime error / no matching output), passes once implemented.
